newsitem.title: UK: Dixons bounces after budget-driven decline.
newsitem.headline: Dixons bounces after budget-driven decline.

text.p: Shares in UK electricals retailer Dixons Group rebounded sharply on Thursday amid perceptions the recent decline was overdone, dealers said.
By 1246 GMT, the shares were up 15-1/2p to 563p.

They tumbled 20p, or 3.5 percent, after Channcellor Kenneth Clarke on Tuesday unveiled his annual budget, which included tax measures that potentially affect insurance policies sold with consumer durable goods.
"I think the whole thing on the downside was overdone," said one marketmaker.
Kingfisher, which also got hit on the budget, bounced 7p to 627-1/2p on Thursday.
"The knee-jerk reaction in Dixons and Kingfisher is probably over cautious and sentiment rather than factually driven," analyst Rowan Morgan of Nikko Europe said in a research report.
